headline: Brigham nurses pause planned strike to vote on hospital’s final contract offer
dek: About 4,000 Boston nurses will review Mass General Brigham’s proposal after the hospital and union reached a late bargaining breakthrough, but a walkout remains possible if members reject the deal.
body: About 4,000 nurses at Brigham and Women’s Hospital in Boston have postponed an open-ended strike that was scheduled to begin Wednesday after Mass General Brigham presented what the hospital called its last, best and final offer. The Massachusetts Nurses Association’s Brigham bargaining committee agreed to withdraw the strike notice and put the proposal before the nurses, according to [the hospital’s statement](https://news.massgeneralbrigham.org/en/bwh-potential-nursing-strike-oct-10) and [CBS Boston](https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/brigham-nurses-strike-postponed/?intcid=CNR-01-0623). The decision changes the immediate outlook for patients and the region’s health-care system, but it does not end the contract dispute.

The agreement was reached after a 13-hour bargaining session on Saturday, Oct. 10, the hospital said. CBS Boston reported that the session was the 27th bargaining meeting between the hospital and the union. The MNA told CBS that the strike was postponed so the 4,000 nurses could study and vote on the offer, describing the contract as complex and saying the nurses would determine their next steps. The [Massachusetts Nurses Association’s public updates](https://www.massnurses.org/news-and-events/) show the dispute had been headed toward an Oct. 14 strike. The sources did not announce when or how the membership vote would be conducted.

The hospital’s proposal would keep a contract in place through Sept. 30, 2028. On wages, the offer would add a 2.5% top step to every covered wage scale when the contract is ratified, then add another 2.5% top step on Sept. 30, 2027. The scales named by Brigham include staff nurses, nurses in charge, midwives, clinical nurse specialists, nurse practitioners, staff education instructors and nurse anesthetists. The hospital separately says nurses progressing through its existing scale would continue to receive annual increases; the union and management have disagreed sharply over how the offer works in practice.

Health insurance is another unresolved point. Under the hospital’s written proposal, only nurses hired into 40-hour positions after ratification who choose individual coverage in the post-tax plan would pay a new 2.5% employee contribution, which Brigham estimates at about $10 a week. The proposal says there would be no higher premium share for nurses already regularly scheduled for 40 hours while they remain in that position, and no increase for nurses enrolled in the post-tax plan. CBS reported that the union has characterized the broader negotiations as a fight over wages and insurance costs, including its allegation that Mass General Brigham sought a multiyear pay freeze. The hospital disputes that characterization and says the nurses would still receive increases as they move through the wage scale.

The offer also addresses staffing practices that affect daily patient care. Brigham says it would create 20 new 36-hour float-pool positions within 60 days of ratification, track floating and agency-nurse use throughout 2027, and provide quarterly data to the MNA. The hospital would also notify the union when an agency nurse, locum, traveler or internal resource-pool nurse works at Brigham for more than six months in a calendar year. For canceled extra or overtime shifts, the proposal calls for at least one hour and 45 minutes’ notice or $70 in pay, with an exception for a canceled shift following a regularly scheduled shift.

The stakes are higher because the nurses and Mass General Brigham already went through a one-day strike in July, followed by a four-day lockout, according to CBS Boston. The MNA had scheduled this week’s action as an indefinite walkout, which would have been more disruptive than the July stoppage. The union has also filed unfair-labor-practice allegations; CBS reported that the hospital denies the allegations, and the hospital’s [Oct. 9 public update](https://news.massgeneralbrigham.org/en/bwh-potential-nursing-strike-oct-9) said they had not been proven or upheld through the legal process.

For now, the practical result is a pause: Brigham nurses are expected to remain at work while the proposed contract goes to a vote. The hospital said its final offer reflects the value of its nurses while balancing patient care, the workforce and the institution’s long-term strength. The union’s vote will determine whether the tentative path becomes a ratified contract or whether the dispute returns to bargaining and a new strike notice becomes possible. CBS reported that any renewed strike would require a new 10-day notice, so the Oct. 14 walkout is no longer the operative schedule.
location: Brigham and Women’s Hospital, Boston, Massachusetts
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Brigham nurses postpone strike to vote on final offer
seoDescription: About 4,000 Brigham nurses postponed a planned open-ended strike while members review Mass General Brigham’s final contract offer.
